title: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 250 mg lebrikizumab in patients with localized scleroderma (LEMO)
official: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 250 mg lebrikizumab in patients with localized scleroderma (LEMO)
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy of 250mg Q2W lebrikizumab compared to a placebo in adult patients with moderate to severe localized scleroderma after 24 weeks.

interventions.name: Ebglyss 250 mg solution for injection in pre-filled syringe

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Signed and dated informed consent has been obtained prior to any protocol-related procedures.
2. Baseline mLossi ≥5
3. Adults, aged ≥18 years
4. Diagnosis of LoS by a specialist with plaque-type or generalized LoS with documented disease activity (increase in size of the lesions and a visible erythema) within the last 6 months and at least one active lesion
5. Insufficient response to potent topical steroid therapy for >3 months
Exclusion criteria:
1. Active rheumatoid arthritis that requires treatment, which interferes with the IMP
2. Intention to use any concomitant medication or therapy that is not permitted by this protocol or failure to undergo the required washout period for a particular prohibited medication
3. Known liver cirrhosis and/or chronic hepatitis of any etiology
4. Pregnant or breastfeeding women, or women planning to become pregnant or breastfeed during the study
5. Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) who are unwilling to practice highly effective contraception prior to the initial dose/start of the first treatment, during the study, and for at least 30 days after the last dose
6. In the Investigator’s opinion, any clinically significant laboratory test results from the chemistry or haematology tests obtained at the Screening visit
7. Potential subjects who are in a dependent/employment relationship with the sponsor, investigator or clinical trial site
8. Potential subjects who are placed in an institution due to a court or official order
9. Active systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) that requires treatment, which interferes with IMP
10. Previous treatment with immunosuppressants, JAK-inhibitors and/or other biologics within the last 8 weeks
11. Previous treatment with topical cortisone, topical calcineurininhibitors and topical vitamin d within the last 2 weeks
12. Severe cardiovascular disease
13. UV therapy within the last 8 weeks
14. Hypersensitivity to the active ingredient or ingredients of the preparation
15. Known current or chronic infections (requiring systemic treatment or with duration above 6 weeks or recurring) e.g., hepatitis virus, or history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection or known positive HIV serology
16. Previous treatment with biologic targeting IL-13 pathway (dupilumab or tralokinumab or lebrikizumab)
